_comment: A2 landscape poster composition layout. All zone rects are Matplotlib figure-fraction coordinates [x, y, width, height], origin at BOTTOM-LEFT of the page (Matplotlib's native convention), so 'y' for a zone near the top of the page is a large number close to 1.0. Editing this file changes the poster layout without touching src/poster.py.
_page: Physical page size in millimeters -- true A2 landscape. width_in/height_in are derived (mm / 25.4) and used directly as the Matplotlib figure size so the composition is real-world-sized for later PDF export.
_v1.1_note: V1.1 revision: main_map grown from height 0.35 to 0.45 (the world map is the hero element and was previously letterboxed inside its zone -- Robinson's ~1.99:1 aspect only used its zone's height, not its width, so growing height alone grows the actual rendered map both taller and wider). insets_row reduced 0.19 -> 0.15 (~21%, within the requested 20-25%). index absorbs the remainder (0.285 -> 0.222); title and footer zones are untouched. Gaps between zones stay a uniform 0.01.
_v1.2_note: V1.2 revision: main_map grown further, 0.45 -> 0.5404, targeting ~450-475mm (75-80%) effective rendered map width. The index column count is capped by a REAL measured constraint, not a guess: the two longest entries ('Democratic Republic of the Congo', 'Saint Vincent and the Grenadines') render at ~48.9mm at 7.6pt, so a column needs >=~58.7mm to avoid colliding with the next column -- at this gap that caps the index at 9 columns / 21 rows, which sets index height's floor. index_missing_note_reserved_fraction (0.077) and index height (0.1701) are solved together so the missing-numbers note has genuine physical clearance below row 21 (~5.5mm) -- an earlier draft of this revision computed the reserved fraction from index height's *fraction* rather than the note's actual physical size, which left too little room and the note visually collided with the last row; this version reserves real inches, not a coincidental percentage. insets_row reduced a further 15% from V1.1 (0.15 -> 0.1275, slightly beyond the suggested 5-10% -- needed to hit the width target once the index's true minimum was accounted for; verified with the marker/collision system afterward, still 0 collisions). Inter-zone gaps tightened 0.007 -> 0.006. title and footer zones remain untouched (same y/height as V1.0/V1.1).

inset_width_weights._comment: Relative width of each inset within the insets row -- Europe is wider because it now carries the Balkan entries in addition to the original microstates.
